title: Quantum cellular automata and invertible phases of matter
authors: Corey Jones, Nikita Sopenko, Ryan Thorngren
abstract: We introduce and study (fermionic and bosonic) invertible quasi-local algebras over uniformly locally finite metric spaces $X$ with infinite-dimensional local von Neumann algebras. We show that the group of Brauer equivalence classes of such algebras is isomorphic to both the group of phases of invertible states and the group of stable equivalence classes of quantum cellular automata over $X\times \mathbb{Z}$. Using K-theory of the symmetric monoidal category of invertible quasi-local algebras and bounded spread isomorphisms, we propose a definition of an $Ω$-spectrum of invertible phases as conjectured by Kitaev. We then show that the $c=\frac{1}{2}$ chiral Majorana fermion net and the $(E_{8})_{1}$ conformal net provide Brauer non-trivial invertible quasi-local algebras, thus providing explicit constructions of non-trivial invertible states and quantum cellular automata on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$. In addition, we show that the time-slice nets of rational diagonal conformal field theories admit lattice degrees of freedom, which implies the discretization of any holomorphic conformal net is invertible.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a deep mathematical connection between three concepts: quantum cellular automata, invertible phases of matter, and the algebraic structure of local observables. By using advanced tools from K-theory and operator algebras, the authors prove these three groups are isomorphic, providing a powerful classification tool for topological phases beyond simple lattice models.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a rigorous mathematical framework for classifying invertible phases of matter and relating them to quantum cellular automata (QCA) using infinite-dimensional local algebras.
main_result: The authors establish isomorphisms between the groups of stable QCA, Brauer equivalence classes of invertible quasi-local algebras, and invertible phases for systems over a metric space X.
method: The methodology involves using K-theory of the symmetric monoidal category of invertible quasi-local algebras and analyzing the algebraic structure of observables derived from conformal field theories.
model_or_system: The study concerns topological phases of matter modeled by quasi-local algebras on infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces, specifically examining chiral conformal nets like the $c=1/2$ Majorana fermion net and the $(E_8)_1$ net.
key_observables: The group of Brauer equivalence classes of invertible quasi-local algebras, the group of stable QCA, and the group of invertible phases.
important_parameters: The dimension of the underlying space (e.g., $\mathbb{Z}^2$), the central charge $c$ of the CFT, and the structure of the metric space $X$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on generalizing to infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces to ensure the isomorphism between QCA and invertible phases holds, contrasting with finite-dimensional cases.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the mathematical maps connecting QCA, Brauer equivalence classes, and invertible phases.
paper_structure: The paper introduces invertible quasi-local algebras, proves the fundamental isomorphism relating QCA, Brauer classes, and invertible phases, defines the $\Omega$-spectrum using K-theory, and concludes with explicit constructions using known CFTs.
why_interesting: It provides deep mathematical connections between algebraic quantum field theory (CFT/QFT), topological order, and discrete symmetries (QCA), which is crucial for understanding the mathematical structure underlying exotic quantum phases.
